Perused the material placed on record including the TCR.
ORDER
ON APPEAL 1.

The present appeal u/s 374 (3) Cr.P.C. has been filed by appellant against the impugned judgment dated 25.10.2018 passed by the Court of Sh. Jitendra Pratap Singh, ld. MM(North), Rohini Courts,
Delhi in case FIR No. 338/2002, PS Bawana, u/s 420/467/468/471/120B IPC, whereby the ld. MM has acquitted all the accused persons of the offences they have been charged with in the present case.

2. It is submitted by ld. counsel for the appellant that the ld. trial Court failed to appreciate the testimony of PW1 Sh. Ram Chander, who was shown as one of the attesting witness of the alleged Will of Late Smt. Ratni Devi.

PW1 Ram Chander categorically deposed during his testimony that Smt. Ratni Devi neither ever executed any Will nor had he signed as attesting witness on the same and that accused Raj Singh obtained his (PW1) signatures on blank papers in April /May 1995 on the false pretext of obtaining loan.

He further submitted that the ld. Trial court erred in finding that testimony of PW1 is not of unimpeachable nature or that signature of PW1 on the Will in question are not disputed but the manner of putting such signatures is in question.

He further submitted that prosecution has unerringly proved through testimony of PW1 Ram Chander, PW19 Insp. Sheoraj Singh that the Will Ex.PW1/A does not bear the thumb impression of late Smt. Ratni Devi.
2.1. He further submitted that ld. MM has failed to appreciate the testimony of independent witnesses namely PW5 Suraj, PW6 Sh. Dalbir, PW7 Kuldeep Singh and PW8 Smt. Roshni Devi.
He has further submitted that PW5 Sh. Suraj deposed that his mother never executed any Will in favour of accused Raj Singh.

Ld. MM did not consider the testimony of PW6 Sh. Dalbir who deposed that in 1997 accused Raj Singh told him that his father had expired and he had to get the land transferred in his (Raj Singh 's) name and therefore requested PW6 to sign on a blank paper, which PW6 did.

He further submitted that ld. MM has also failed to consider the testimony of PW7 Kuldeep Singh who deposed that Smt.Ratni Devi died intestate in the year 1989 and accused forged her Will in the year 1995 and on the basis of the forged Will, the accused Raj Singh got mutation done in his name of the share of land of Smt. Ratni Devi and wrongly obtained compensation from the Government.

He further argued that ld. Trial Court did not consider the testimony of PW8 Smt. Roshni Devi,
daughter of Late Smt. Ratni Devi, who deposed that no Will was ever executed by her mother in favour of accused Sh. Raj Singh.

2.2. He argued that ld. Trial Court did not appreciate deposition of PW11 Smt. Rita Devi that she had not taken any loan from accused Raj Singh and he had wrongly stated on an affidavit filed before the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi that she had taken a loan of Rs.1,50,000/- from accused Raj Singh.

He further submitted that all the PWs proved that late Smt.Ratni Devi never executed any Will and their versions remained unshaken during cross-examination, however, ld. Trial Court erred in ignoring their testimonies.

2.3. He further argued that FSL report Ex.PW15/G nowhere suggests that the analysis was not done by the expert on the basis of comparing the original thumb impression with the forged thumb Kuldeep Singh Sherawat vs State on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168891461/
2 impression on the will.
Ld. counsel further argued that fingerprint expert adopted the correct approach by analyzing the two fingerprints and gave his report which is correct and admissible.

He further argued that the ld. Trial court erred in holding that PW19 could not be called as an expert as per Section 45 of Evidence Act since he possessed no Diploma or Degree from any recognised university in the field of comparing finger prints.

He further argued that no suggestion was put to PW19 regarding him not having training regarding analysing and comparing fingerprints nor any suggestion put to this witness regarding his technique of comparison of finger prints.

2.4. Ld. counsel further argued that ld. Trial Court ignored Ex.DW1/X4 and Ex.DW1/X5 which are the affidavit and declaration of Sh. Surender Kumar (Notary) in which, after seeing the Will of Smt.
Ratni Devi he stated that the said Will was neither executed before him nor did he attest the said Will.
He argued that the said documents are admissible under Section 32 of Indian Evidence Act.

2.5. Ld. counsel further argued that there are other evidences of forgery which are ignored by ld.
Trial Court.

It is submitted by ld. counsel that in the Will, the name of the husband is shown as 'Karne' whereas, in documents proved by DW1 i.e. Ex. D1/27, and Ex.DW1/P3 to Ex.DW1/P6, the name of the husband of late Smt. Ratni Devi is recorded as 'Sh. Karan Singh'.
He further argued that document Ex.DW1/X3 which was initially issued in the name of one Deepak S/o Sultan singh which had subsequently been struck off and replaced by Ratni W /o Karne.
The accused DW1 failed to provide any explanation for the striking off and of the different entry on the death certificate.
He further argued that Ex. DW1/P10 clearly states that death certificate of Smt. Ratni was not available in PGI Rohtak.
He stated that accused Raj Singh not only forged the Will of Ratni but also forged her death certificate.

2.6. He has placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of "Jaspal Singh & Ors. v.
State of Punjab, 20.04.1979", Criminal Appeal Nos. 275 of 1973 and 84 of 1975 3.

sentences.text: On the other hand, ld. counsels for the respondents submitted that the present appeal has been filed by the appellant only to harass the respondents.
Ld. counsels further submitted that order passed by the ld. Trial Court is correct according to the facts of the case.
Hence, the appeal is not maintainable and is liable to be dismissed.

4. Heard.
5.
There is a cardinal difference between the standard of proof required for civil and criminal cases.
In civil trial, case has to be proved on the principle of 'Preponderence of Probabilities' while in the criminal trial, case has to be proved 'beyond reasonable doubt'.
In criminal cases, serious consequences follow and that is why higher level of evidence is required to prove the case.
It is also pertinent to mention here that in criminal cases the burden to prove the case always rests on the prosecution unlike civil cases.

sentences.text: A lot of stress has been put by ld.
Counsel for the appellant on the testimony of PW1 Ram Chander, one of the attesting witness of the Will.
He argued that PW1 during his testimony stated that no Will had been executed by Ms. Ratni Devi in his presence.
PW 1 also stated that his signatures were obtained on some blank and certain typed papers by the accused Raj Singh.
He also stated that he did not know any Ratni.
PW1 admitted during his cross-examination by ld. Addl. PP that he had signed the blank document Ex.PW1/A under the impression that Raj Singh required the same for obtaining loan from the bank.
He also admitted that in his presence Ratni Devi has never executed any Will nor he had signed as attesting witness on the same.
Therefore, court has not rightly upheld his testimony and does not declare forgery on the alleged will.
PW1 Sh. Ram Chander had admitted his signatures in his testimony though he is denying the presence of Smt. Ratni Devi and contents of the documents.

The relevant portion of his testimony is reproduced herein:
"...mere sign kuch kagaz type the kuch kagaz safed the jin par mere sign karaye the.
Un kagazo par Raj ne vasiyat ban wali.
Weh galat hai mere samne Ratni ne koi vasiyat nahi banwai na he mere samne anguthe lagaye.
Yeh vasiyat galat hai na mein Ratni ko janta"

In this regard, ld. MM has rightly observed as under:
"......The signatures of the said witness on the Will in question are not disputed however, it is the manner of the witness putting such signatures which is in question.
The prosecution states that the signatures were obtained on blank documents on the pretext of the accused Raj Singh applying for a loan.
This court finds itself unable to accept this justification as there appears no valid or believable reason for the witness to sign blank documents merely on the asking of accused Raj Singh.
There also does not appear any sufficient cause as to why the signatures of the said witness was required for the accused Raj Singh applying for the loan.
The prosecution has not explained the relationship of the witness with the accused Raj Singh which led him to sign the blank documents merely on asking of accused Raj Singh....."

"....As far as the denial of this witness appearing before the Notary Public for singing the impugned Will is concerned, the same has remained unsubstantiated as the Notary Public could not be examined in court due to his demise.

However, the fact that the relevant document including the register and the sample seal of the concerned Notary Public have not been seized by the IO from the office of Notary Public relating to the Will in question which could connect the witness to the Will in question creates a doubt in the case of the prosecution...."
Reasoning given by ld. MM is quite justified in the given circumstances.

sentences.text: A stress has also been put by ld.
Counsel for the appellant on the testimony of PW19 Insp. Sheoraj Singh, Senior Finger Print Expert.

It is argued by ld. counsel for the appellant that fingerprint expert science is a correct science and the ld. MM had erred in finding that the finger print expert had compared thumb impression on two photocopy documents with each other and did not have the opportunity to see the original of the documents stated to be containing original disputed and admitted thumb impression.
It is admitted fact that this witness was only provided with photocopies of the will as well as the admitted documents i.e. mortgage deed.
Moreover, he has also admitted that he has not gone through any kind of diploma.

The relevant portion of his testimony is as under:
"....On that day my office Dealing clerk handed over to me disputing documents i.e.
Deed of Will made and executed on 14.04.1989 by Smt. Ratri D/o Late Data Ram and W/o sh. Karny in favour of Raj Singh bearing question thumb impression marked Q1 and Q2, rehnama bearing admitted thumb impression marked A1 to A7 of Smt. Ratri W/o Sh. Karny alongwith photographs admitted prints marked A1 to A7 supplied by the IO....."
"....No. I was a science graduate at the time of recruitment...."

In this regard, the ld. MM has rightly observed as under:
"......A perusal of the FSL report Ex.PW15/G would reveal that the opinion in the said report was based on the analysis done by the said PW-19 of the purported thumb impressions of Smt. Ratni available on the photocopy of the impugned Will which is shown to be having the disputed thumb impressions at point Q1 and Q2 thereon.
The comparison was made with alleged admitted thumb impressions (A1 to A7) available on the coloured photocopy of the mortgage deed.
Thus, the finger print expert had compared thumb impressions on two photocopy documents with each other.

In view of this court, such a comparison cannot form the basis of the conviction of accused persons when the expert did not have the opportunity to see the original of the documents stated to be containing disputed and admitted thumb impressions.

In addition thereto, the fact that the witness PW-19 admittedly has not attended any professional Dipolma or Degree course from any recognized university or institute in the field of comparing finger prints and he admittedly, was a simple science Graduate, in view of this court, is not sufficient to bring this witness into the category of experts as provided u/s 45 of the Indian Evidence Act......."

8. It is argued by ld. counsel for the appellant that accused had filed the forged death certificate of Smt. Ratni Devi wherein the name of her husband has been mentioned as Karne whereas her husband name is Karan Singh.
It was incumbent upon the appellant to produce the witness from the PGI Rohtak with the relevant record in this regard.
This fact also not proved beyond reasonable doubt.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The reasoning given by ld. MM in this regard that "... it is not believable that when creating a forged death certificate, the accused would be mentioning incorrect name of the husband of Smt. Ratni therein....."

also seems to be sustainable.
9.
The appellant has placed reliance on Ex.DW1/P2 which is allegedly stated to be the affidavit given by the notary who had executed the impugned Will.
In the regard, the ld. MM had considered that the stamps kept by the notary were necessary to be proved before the Court but the IO had not seized them.
In such circumstances, no much reliance could be placed on the affidavit of the alleged notary.
The reasons given by the ld. MM are as per legal principles and ld. MM has correctly appreciated the evidence.
10. Other witnesses are not of much material.
In the given circumstances, there are lots of doubt remaining regarding forgery having been committed by the respondent.
Considering the overall facts and circumstances, the impugned judgment dated 25.10.2018 is upheld.
Hence, the present appeal is dismissed.

11. Let copy of this order be sent to ld. Trial Court alongwith TCR.
12.
Appeal file be consigned to Record Room.
